Kavarskas Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Utenos apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. This is the older of Kavarskas's two Jewish cemeteries, predating the New cemetery established in 1892, documented elsewhere in this collection, per the Kultūros Vertybių Registras. Jews began settling in Kavarskas in the 18th century, reaching 979 people (63 percent) by 1897, and supported a Jewish congregation with its own rabbi by the late 19th century. Expelled by the retreating Russian army in 1915, only about half the community returned after WWI. When the Germans invaded in 1941, Lithuanian nationalists murdered 30 Jewish men and women even before German troops reached the town; the rest were transferred to Ukmergė and shot on September 5, 1941.
